log.msg: Cross-check passed: two independent counts of real owner messages agree exactly at 48 -- the say.mjs 'heard' tool calls found in the fast assistant's own session transcript (ae22125c-...jsonl), and the owner-authored cards in board.jsonl. Both differ from the raw 53 chat lines in mastermind-layout-browser/task.jsonl by the same 5 messages, all in the relay's first 17 minutes (15:36-15:53) before the heard-card habit had started -- explained, not a measurement error.

Five hops measured from real jsonl records, no synthetic run staged. said->arrived is near-zero and unmeasured (no arrival hook wired). arrived->echoed/carded median 3.9s (the assistant noticing and logging). echoed/carded->relayed median 0.0s (same write, same command). relayed->picked-up median 52s in a live conversational session. picked-up->visible median 1676s (about 28 minutes) -- mostly real agent work, measured directly from dispatch/landing pairs in mastermind-sonnet-run and mastermind-layout-browser task logs.

Attack-first recommendation: relayed->picked-up, not the biggest number. Tonight's autonomous mastermind-sonnet-run shows a real ~34-minute gap (20:15 to 20:49) with nothing in flight and no one checking the inbox, because it wakes on a timer rather than on arrival. A message landing in that window would wait up to half an hour before anyone even looks at it -- exactly the owner's 'should never queue' complaint -- and the fix (check the inbox the moment a chat line lands, not just at the next scheduled wakeup) is a small process change. picked-up->visible is 15-30x bigger in the median but is mostly real work (an agent reading, writing, and checking code) that cannot be cut for free.
